incidents.victim: North American academic, medical & military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploited externally facing REDCap research servers, deployed custom 'INFINITERED' malware to harvest credentials, then pivoted to a domain admin account and abused domain content-compliance rules to covertly forward emails.
incidents.impact: Sweeping intelligence collection across medical, AI, cyber and national-defense research went undetected for over a year (Sept 2023-Nov 2025) before Google/Mandiant disrupted it and notified affected organizations.

incidents.vector: Abused the AUR 'adopt orphaned package' mechanism to seize maintainership of abandoned packages and inject a malicious npm package (later swapped for a Bun script to evade detection) that installed a rootkit and infostealer.
incidents.impact: More than 1,900 community packages hijacked over a weekend to deploy a rootkit and credential/secret-stealing malware; affected users urged to rotate all passwords and tokens.

incidents.victim: WordPress sites using OptinMonster, TrustPulse & PushEngage
incidents.vector: Compromised plugin developer Awesome Motive and added malicious JavaScript to three legitimate plugins that waits for an admin login, creates a rogue admin account, then installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million websites backdoored through trusted plugin updates, granting attackers persistent administrative access.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed cyberattack; the company has shared no technical details, and Russian government agencies are involved in the investigation.
incidents.impact: Roughly a week of outages across tax-reporting, electronic document management, cash register and authentication services used by Russian government agencies, banks and state enterprises; no customer data confirmed leaked.

incidents.victim: Polish public figures and their families
incidents.vector: Phishing pages (with near-daily new domains) targeting personal Gmail accounts to steal login credentials and two-factor authentication codes.
incidents.impact: CERT Polska warned that the long-running GhostWriter operation expanded from work accounts to personal Gmail of officials, researchers, journalists and law enforcement, plus their relatives, to harvest contacts and sensitive documents.

incidents.victim: State of Maine data breach portal
incidents.vector: Submitted fake breach notices on forged corporate letterhead through a public portal that accepted filings with no verification.
incidents.impact: Bogus breach reports for VRChat (falsely claiming 2.4M affected) and Discord forced Maine to take its public-facing breach database offline pending a procedural audit, cutting off a resource used by researchers and journalists.

incidents.victim: Council of Europe, Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar, University of Nottingham
incidents.vector: Exploited an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft ERP zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, added to CISA's KEV catalog) to steal large volumes of data.
incidents.impact: The ShinyHunters group listed a fresh wave of extortion victims; the University of Nottingham alone had 40GB and data on 450,000+ students and alumni stolen.

incidents.vector: Data stolen from a third-party supplier and used as leverage for an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: The Shadowbyt3$ group is seeking a $2 million ransom, claiming to have stolen nearly 1GB of employee and business data.

incidents.vector: Conti ransomware deployed to hack victim networks, encrypt data and steal files, demanding ransom to restore access and avoid public disclosure.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty after extradition from Ireland; Conti hit 1,000+ networks across 47 states and 31 countries, yielding at least $150M in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to parts of the internal network; the company took systems offline to investigate and evict them.
incidents.impact: The Danish pharma giant (maker of Ozempic and Wegovy) confirmed some sensitive data, including patient PII, was copied during the intrusion.

incidents.vector: Compromised a developer laptop and stole private multisig keys.
incidents.impact: Roughly $36 million in crypto-assets stolen; the Humanity token lost nearly 90% of its value shortly after the hack.

incidents.vector: Data allegedly stolen from a government agency managing healthcare entitlements, then offered on online black markets.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens allegedly exposed; the government has launched a probe.

incidents.vector: Suspected Russian intrusion into the congressman's Signal account; the FBI notified him this week.
incidents.impact: Compromise of the Signal account of a senior US lawmaker who is a vocal Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack that forced a halt to operational technology and milling processes.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer paused cane haulage and milling at two Mackay-region mills at the start of the crushing season.

incidents.vector: At least 13 fake consulting-company websites with AI-generated personas and photos posted bogus 'consulting' jobs on hiring platforms to recruit current and former clearance holders, pressuring them via encrypted apps to share insider information for payment.
incidents.impact: The DOJ and FBI seized the 13 domains used by suspected Chinese agents to lure Americans with access to classified information; payments were laundered through cryptocurrency and overseas accounts.

incidents.vector: A CISA contractor intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and a large trove of other agency secrets to a public GitHub account.
incidents.impact: Lawmakers are demanding answers as CISA struggles to contain the exposure and invalidate the leaked credentials.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing operation luring targeted users into clicking malicious links sent via WhatsApp that redirected them to an external site.
incidents.impact: Meta says it disrupted the campaign and filed for contempt, alleging NSO violated a US court injunction barring it from targeting WhatsApp; Meta urged lawmakers to keep NSO sanctions in place.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of PAN-OS authentication-bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 in the GlobalProtect portal and gateway to initiate unauthorized VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed probing and a small number of successful gateway-connected sessions; no post-access lateral movement seen yet. CVE added to CISA's KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: Confidential client data stolen from an external cloud storage site, followed by an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: The major US law firm reportedly paid an estimated $20 million to the Silent Ransom Group to prevent release of stolen data; the FBI has warned the group is specifically targeting US law firms.

incidents.vector: Google Ads malvertising distributed via shell companies delivered fake desktop apps (podcast player, PDF viewers) carrying the new 'FlutterShell' backdoor, which uses a WebView/JavaScript bridge to run attacker-hosted logic and weaponizes AI summarization features for data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Operation FlutterBridge (cluster CL-CRI-1089) spread adware with full backdoor capabilities — shell command execution and file-system access — through notarized, validly signed apps with zero VirusTotal detections.

incidents.vector: A compromised Red Hat employee GitHub account pushed malicious orphan commits that triggered CI/CD pipelines to publish trojanized packages with valid SLSA provenance, delivering the 'Miasma' payload (Mini Shai-Hulud lineage).
incidents.impact: At least 32 packages (~80,000 weekly downloads) backdoored to steal GitHub/npm/SSH tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, Kubernetes and Vault secrets and CI/CD secrets; part of an accelerating wave of self-replicating npm supply-chain worms.

incidents.victim: High-value Instagram accounts (incl. Obama White House, US Space Force)
incidents.vector: Tricked Meta's AI support assistant into adding an attacker-controlled email to target accounts during the password-reset flow, using a VPN with an IP near the target's hometown; accounts with MFA enabled were not affected.
incidents.impact: Pro-Iran hackers briefly defaced high-profile Instagram accounts and hijacked valuable short usernames; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.
